package_info.why_malicious: These packages are considered malicious because they are mass-uploaded spam and phishing packages designed to manipulate search engine results (SEO), mislead users, and potentially direct them to phishing or scam sites via obfuscated or shortener-based URLs. The packages serve no legitimate software purpose and pollute the npm registry.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code redirects the user's browser to a shortened URL, which may lead to a phishing or scam site, resulting in user redirection and potential credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting users to external URLs, especially via shorteners, is a common phishing and scam tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not perform browser redirects or force navigation to external sites upon import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use URL shorteners for documentation links, but not for forced redirects.
key_indicators: Use of URL shorteners (e.g., bit.ly) in code

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: console.log('Check out John Wick at https://tinyurl.com/4example');
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code prints a message containing a shortened URL to the console, potentially luring users to visit a phishing or scam site.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encouraging users to visit obfuscated URLs is a social engineering tactic to bypass URL reputation checks and lure victims.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not promote unrelated external links, especially via shorteners, in their output.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may print documentation or support links, but not unrelated or obfuscated URLs.
key_indicators: Promotion of unrelated or suspicious external links

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Visit https://bit.ly/3example for more John Wick content!
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (or when viewing package metadata), the package description or README contains a shortened URL, enticing users to visit potentially malicious sites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding obfuscated URLs in package metadata is a tactic to evade automated scanners and trick users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package metadata should not contain unrelated or obfuscated links.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may link to documentation, but not via shorteners or to unrelated content.
key_indicators: Shortened URLs in README or description
Irrelevant or misleading content in package metadata

attack_chain.action: User or bot discovers the package via npm search or homepage due to SEO manipulation.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is enticed to view or install the package.

attack_chain.action: User views README or description and sees a shortened URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: User may click the link, leading to a phishing or scam site.

attack_chain.action: If the package is installed or imported, code executes to redirect the browser or print a phishing link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected or lured to visit a malicious site, potentially resulting in credential theft or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of URL shorteners (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.) in code or metadata
Immediate browser redirection on import or install
Console output promoting unrelated or obfuscated URLs
High volume of similar packages with spammy or SEO-focused content
file_indicators: index.js or main entrypoint containing window.location.href assignments
README.md or package.json description with shortened URLs
Packages with non-functional or irrelevant code except for link promotion
network_indicators: Outbound requests or redirects to URL shortener domains
Links resolving to recently registered or low-reputation domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package code and metadata for the presence of URL shorteners and forced browser redirects. Flag packages that print or promote unrelated external links, especially via obfuscated URLs. Monitor for high volumes of similar packages with SEO-focused or spammy content. Use reputation checks on linked domains and shorteners to identify potential phishing or scam destinations.
